comparisons.peer_topic: Affordable Housing Investment Performance and Commitments
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation held $16.7 billion in affordable housing equity investments (including $7.5 billion in probable unfunded contributions) at year-end 2024, recognizing $2.2 billion in tax benefits and reporting $1.6 billion in pretax losses in 2024, with potential additional support for troubled projects not expected to be significant.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose specific unfunded commitments associated with their affordable housing and tax credit investments, presenting them as accrued obligations expected to be funded in the near term. GS reported $2.15 billion in accrued unfunded commitments as of Dec 2024, with a majority expected to be funded by year-end 2026. BAC reported $7.5 billion in probable unfunded contributions at year-end 2024, also noting they are probable to be paid over the next five years. While both track similar obligations, BAC's commitment size ($7.5B) is significantly larger than GS's ($2.15B), and BAC explicitly mentions the potential for additional support for troubled projects, whereas GS focuses on the timing of funding for the accrued commitments.

sentences.text: In the table above, investments included $2.15 billion as of December 2024 and $2.26 billion as of December 2023 of accrued unfunded commitments.
As of December 2024, a majority of such accrued unfunded commitments were expected to be funded by year-end 2026.

The Corporation's equity investments in affordable housing and other projects totaled $16.7 billion and $15.8 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023, which included unfunded capital contributions of $7.5 billion and $7.2 billion that are probable to be paid over the next five years.
The Corporation may be asked to invest additional amounts to support a troubled affordable housing project.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of ASU No. 2023-02 for Tax Credit Structures
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for certain tax-incentivized investments, which had no material impact on the financial statements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi disclose the adoption of accounting guidance (ASU No. 2023-02) allowing the use of the proportional amortization method for tax credit structures. GS presents investments meeting these criteria in a table and discusses accrued unfunded commitments. Citi explicitly states it adopted ASU No. 2023-02 effective January 1, 2024, which expanded the scope of eligible investments and permits the use of the proportional amortization method. Both disclosures center on the operationalization and accounting treatment of tax-incentivized investments under this specific method.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adoption of proportional amortization method expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Effective January 1, 2024, the Firm expanded its use of the proportional amortization method to cover tax-oriented investments beyond affordable housing, allowing program-by-program election.

JPM explicitly adopted updates to the guidance effective January 1, 2024, expanding the types of eligible investments beyond affordable housing and allowing program-by-program elections. Both companies are aligning their accounting for similar tax credit assets under the proportional amortization framework.
